key_insight: Bayesian inference fused with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade—at the electron/hole transport interfaces or in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted durability improvements by identifying the specific interfaces and regions that most strongly limit long-term device stability.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to experimental observations
Bayesian inference to generate spatially resolved parameter maps and track them during aging
evidence_signal: The inferred parameter maps were tracked under accelerated aging conditions (70 °C, full-spectrum sunlight) and showed strong spatially non-uniform degradation, with the largest changes concentrated at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The approach depends on the fidelity of the physical model and imaging-to-parameter inference, so mis-specified recombination or transport assumptions could bias the inferred degradation origin.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
